title: Black queer men in Lewisham | BLKOUT in Lewisham
metaDescription: For Black queer men in and around Lewisham — Deptford, Catford, New Cross, Brockley: what's here, what's beside us, what's worth the journey, and a community-owned door into BLKOUT.

landmark.alt: Pencil sketch of The Albany, Deptford, with the BLKOUT roundel as a moon above it

hero.kicker: One community. Many doors. This one is Lewisham's.
hero.heading: BLKOUT in Lewisham
hero.standfirst: BLKOUT is a community-owned co-operative for Black queer men across the UK — and Lewisham holds a building we keep coming back to. The Albany in Deptford has hosted our own event series, a play we supported, and a Black Gay Ink writers' event we spoke at. In April 2023 we put out a direct call-out — #StrongerTogether — to Black bi, gay and/or trans men across the borough, to co-create a peer support project for each other's mental health. Around 81,900 Black residents live here. This door is for the Black queer men among them.

here.heading: Here in Lewisham
here.intro: In April 2023 we put out a direct call-out to Black bi, gay and/or trans men in Lewisham to co-create a peer support project together. We don't have a public record of what came of it — help us find out, or help us restart it.
here.quietNote: Nothing else is listed in Lewisham right now beyond the directory below — checked 31 August 2026. That's a report, not a silence. The door below is always open.

worthTheJourney.heading: Worth the journey
worthTheJourney.intro: Black queer men have never let a borough boundary decide where community happens. Where you're centred, not just welcome:

entries.note: A genuine Black-queer-centred mental health programme, one borough over in neighbouring Lambeth.

services.heading: Look after yourself
services.intro: Free, confidential, no GP needed, no judgement — and your business stays yours.

entries.title: Black Gay Ink
entries.author: Troy Fairclough, with Spread the Word
entries.note: A writing development scheme for Black gay men, funded by Arts Council England — ran workshops and showcases at The Albany, Deptford, including at the 2024 Deptford Literature Festival, before evolving into Black Rainbow Ink. BLKOUT spoke at one of its Albany events.

numbers.heading: The numbers nobody counts
numbers.body: The 2021 Census counted around 81,900 Black residents in Lewisham — the third-largest Black population of any London borough. On the estimates we publish, that's 1,800 to 2,600 Black queer men living here right now. These are working estimates and we welcome correction. The point is the scale: we were never a niche. We were just never counted.
numbers.history:
Lewisham's Black queer history is quieter in the public record than its numbers deserve — and where it exists, it's mostly ours to tell, and it mostly runs through one building.

The Albany, Deptford's community arts centre, has hosted us more than once. In 2016, BlackOutUK ran a series called E-troducing there. Over the years since, we've also supported a play staged at The Albany, and spoken at an event run by Black Gay Ink — Troy Fairclough's writing development scheme for Black gay men, which held workshops and showcases there into the mid-2020s before evolving into Black Rainbow Ink. And in April 2023, BLKOUT put out a direct call-out — #StrongerTogether — to Black bi, gay and/or trans men in Lewisham more widely: get together, get support from local professionals, decide what would work for you. 'Your crown has been bought and paid for.' We don't have a public record of what that group went on to do, which is exactly the kind of thing this page exists to find out.

What's real and building now: Deptford's Piehouse Co-op — a railway arch venue that closed and was fought back open by its community in November 2024 — and a council-backed capacity-building project launching in April 2026, explicitly prioritising Black and racially minoritised LGBTQ+ people as it rebuilds the borough's LGBT+ network. The infrastructure is arriving. If you were part of the 2023 group, on that stage, or in that writers' room — the panel below is where you tell us.

archive.intro: Lewisham doesn't yet have a piece in our published story archive — but our 2023 #StrongerTogether call-out and the 2016 E-troducing series at The Albany are both real, and belong here once we've brought that record back online.

faq.q: Where can I meet other Black queer men in Lewisham?
faq.a: We called for one to form in April 2023, and we're honest that we don't have a public record of what came of it — start with the door on this page, and BLKOUT's national community is open to you today. If a few Lewisham men want a table in the borough, we'll help hold it.

faq.q: Where can I get an STI test or PrEP in Lewisham?
faq.a: Sexual Health London posts free test kits and PrEP to any London address, no GP and no conversation required. 56 Dean Street is a short ride away in Soho.

BLKOUT is one community-owned co-operative for Black queer men across the UK — with a door in every borough. We're registered in Croydon and we belong wherever our men are. We ran events in Lewisham a decade before this page existed.

faq.q: I'm not out. Can I still come?
faq.a: Yes. Come as you are — nobody at this door asks you to be anything first, and your business stays yours.

faq.q: Is the history on this page accurate?
faq.a: It's checked against the public record and dated so you can see when we last looked — and where we couldn't find something, we've said so rather than guessed. If we've got something wrong, or you were part of a chapter we've missed, the panel at the bottom is where you tell us, and the page changes.

door.heading: Be met
door.tender: Come as you are. We answer.
door.intro: Leave your name and we'll keep you posted about Lewisham — what's on, what's starting, and how to be part of it. This goes to BLKOUT, a co-operative owned by its members. No engagement machinery, nothing sold onward — just a community that answers.

truer.heading: Make it truer
truer.intro: We know this page is thinner than Lewisham deserves — and the people here know the rest of it. If there's a group we've missed, a chapter of our own history you were part of, or something building we haven't heard about — tell us. Corrections get credited, if you want the credit.

footer.line: BLKOUT is a member-owned Community Benefit Society for Black queer men in the UK. One platform, many doors — this one is Lewisham's.
